title: Decide and document whether the OIDC handler may keep its non-standard response shape
goal: The OIDC handler writes six raw c.JSON responses instead of using common.Success and common.Fail, which looks like the same drift the tenant handler has. It may not be drift: OIDC endpoints are consumed by an identity provider and by standards-aware clients, and wrapping a token response in a business envelope would break them. This wave is an investigation with an evidence-backed decision as its deliverable: for each of the six responses, identify the protocol contract it belongs to, and either keep it raw with a comment naming the contract, or move it onto the common envelope if it is genuinely a business endpoint. No code change is required if every response turns out to be protocol-shaped.
findings: RC-026 (P3): backend/modules/auth/oidc/handler.go:28,46,55,63,88,94 write raw c.JSON while the rest of the codebase uses the common envelope.
Unknown: whether each of the six responses is part of an OIDC protocol contract (authorization code, token, userinfo, discovery) or a business endpoint that merely lives in this handler.

in: Classify each of the six raw responses against its protocol contract
Add a one-line comment naming the contract for each response that must stay raw
Move any response that is genuinely a business endpoint onto common.Success / common.Fail
Record the classification table in evidence
out: Changing any OIDC response body, status, header or field name
Changing the OIDC callback URL, state handling, nonce handling or token validation

implementationNotes: Default to keep. An identity provider is not a party that can be asked to change its parser, so a protocol response that is raw today stays raw unless it is provably a business endpoint.
The deliverable is the classification, not a diff. A wave that changes nothing and documents why is a successful wave.
If any endpoint is business-shaped, changing it requires a matching frontend change and belongs in its own commit with a response diff.
Do not use this wave to touch the tenant handler envelope; that is a separate S2 packet.

executionRoles.implementerPosture: Classify first; only change responses proven to be business endpoints.
reviewerPosture: Check each classification against the protocol spec, not against intuition.
Check every surviving raw response has a contract comment.
Check the OIDC end-to-end login still works.

runtimeEvidence: one OIDC login round-trip against the configured provider, or an explicit runtime gap naming the missing provider

evidenceRequired: .harness/evidence/2026-10-27-s3-oidc-envelope/classification.md with one row per raw response
humanGates: Confirm any proposed envelope change for an OIDC endpoint; the default decision is keep raw.
completionChecklist: All six raw responses are classified
Every surviving raw response names its protocol contract in a comment
OIDC login still works or the runtime gap is recorded
